text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- 16 members of security forces injured in clashes in Deir Alla after people protest destruction of illegal houses.
- State engineers to get pay bonuses from next year.
- Jordan and Kuwait to resume flights for first time since 1990-91 Gulf crisis. Foreign ministers of Jordan and Kuwait discuss ties by phone.
- King Hussein to meet British Prime Minister Tony Blair on Thursday.
- Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawneh says expects full relations with Kuwait to be resumed within weeks.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali proposes investment projects to Sheikh Zayed in Abu Dhabi and says Jordan ready to provide labour force to work in the emirates.
- Interior ministry source says Jordanian elections set for November 18th.
- Deputy Prime Minister Jawad al-Anani denies Al-Arab Al-Yawm report of arrests of infiltrators in Jordan.
- Jordan and Iraq hold talks on practical implementation of annual trade protocol and Iraqi oil exports to Jordan.
- Jordanian securities broker expects $400 million of international investment in Jordanian shares by the end of the year in the form of global share issues and corporate bonds.
- Professional union presidents not to resign over new press law.
- Opposition calls for extraordinary session of parliament but get only 27 parliamentary signatures on their petition -- 14 short of the number needed to be accepted.
